rounds.proof_sketch: With fixed input shape [128,1], size=128. The kernel launches 1 block of 256 threads. Thread 255 has idx=255 >= size=128, so thread_loss=0.0f. The mutation reduces shared_mem from [256] to [255], causing OOB access at index 255. However, thread 255 writes 0.0f to shared_mem[255], and thread 127 reads from shared_mem[255] during reduction (stride=128). Since the value is always 0.0f, the addition has no effect on the result regardless of memory behavior.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation introduces an out-of-bounds access at shared_mem[255], but this is unreachable by meaningful computation under the fixed input shape. With size=128, threads 128-255 all have thread_loss=0.0f because their idx >= size condition fails. Thread 255 always writes 0.0f to the OOB location, and thread 127 reads this during the first reduction step (adding shared_mem[127+128]). Since 0.0f is being written and read, the out-of-bounds access cannot affect the numerical result. The underlying hardware appears to have sufficient physical memory at the OOB location (likely due to alignment/padding), so no crash occurs. To kill this mutant would require input size >= 256 where thread 255 has a non-zero contribution, but shape changes are forbidden.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. Thread 255 always has idx >= size (255 >= 128), so thread_loss is always 0.0f. The OOB write/read at index 255 always involves 0.0f, which has no effect on the sum. Killing would require size >= 256 to give thread 255 meaningful work, but input shapes are fixed.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for shared memory size changes should include shape variations as part of the test suite. For fixed-shape contracts, consider flagging shared memory mutations as potentially equivalent when the mutation affects indices beyond the actual data size. Additionally, this type of undefined behavior mutation should be paired with memory sanitizer testing to detect OOB accesses even when they produce 'correct' results.
